Raphaëlle: French feminine of Raphaël, from Hebrew 'God has healed'. Raphael is an archangel.
Assiya: Arabic Asiya, 'healer' or 'one who tends the wounded'. Name of the Pharaoh's righteous wife in Islamic tradition.
Ivy: English, from the climbing plant ivy, from Old English ifig. Associated with fidelity.
Elsa: Short form of Elisabeth, Hebrew 'my God is an oath'. Also Germanic 'noble'.
Odile: French, from Germanic aud 'wealth' and a diminutive. Saint Odilia is patron of Alsace.
Ilyes: Arabic and Berber form of Elias, from Hebrew 'my God is Yahweh'.
Célestin: French, from Latin caelestinus, 'heavenly'. Name of several popes.
Nael: Arabic, 'one who attains' or 'acquirer'. Also used as a Breton form of Noël in rare cases.
Armand: French form of Herman, from Germanic hari 'army' and man.
Maeve: Anglicised Irish Medb, 'she who intoxicates' or 'mead'. A queen in Irish legend.
Zeynep: Turkish form of Arabic Zaynab, possibly from 'fragrant tree' or 'father's jewel'.
Coco: French nickname, originally a pet form of Nicole or Chanel's nickname. Also a Spanish and Portuguese pet name.
Amine: Arabic Amin, 'trustworthy, faithful'. French spelling of the same name.
Celine: Variant of Céline, from Latin Caelina, 'heavenly' root caelum.
Azra: Arabic, 'virgin' or 'pure'. Common in Turkey and the Balkans.
Angelina: Italian and Spanish diminutive of Angela, from Greek angelos 'messenger'.
Joseph: Hebrew Yosef, 'he will add'. Biblical son of Jacob.
Roxanne: Persian Roshanak, 'dawn' or 'little star'. Wife of Alexander the Great.
Raphael: Hebrew, 'God has healed'. One of the archangels.
Léonore: French form of Eleanor or Leonora. Probably from Provençal Aliénor, origin uncertain.
Alessia: Italian feminine of Alessio, from Greek 'defender'.
Maëlys: Modern Breton and French name, probably from Maël 'prince' blended with a suffix. Origin uncertain.
Asya: Turkish form of Asia, Arabic 'healer'. Also a Russian form of Anastasia.
Talia: Hebrew 'dew from God', or Greek 'blooming', from the Muse Thalia.
Myla: Probably a modern variant of Mila or Mylah, possibly from 'merciful' or 'dear'. Origin uncertain.
Alexia: Feminine form of Alexios, from Greek alexein 'to defend'.
Charline: French feminine diminutive of Charles, from Germanic karl 'free man'.
Yousra: Arabic, 'ease, prosperity'. A Quranic concept of facility.
Jasmine: From Persian yasmin, the fragrant flower. Also used in Arabic and English.
Hassan: Arabic, 'handsome, good'. Grandson of the Prophet Muhammad.
Darius: Latin form of Persian Dariush, 'holder of the good'. Name of Achaemenid kings.
Alparslan: Turkish, 'heroic lion', from alp 'hero' and arslan 'lion'. Name of a Seljuk sultan.
Yaman: Turkish and Arabic, 'Yemen' or 'right side, good fortune'. Also used as 'brave'.
Jonas: Greek and Latin form of Jonah, Hebrew 'dove'.
Rune: Scandinavian, from Old Norse run 'secret, mystery'. Also the letters of the ancient Germanic alphabet.
Eliot: English and French, from Elias or Ellis, Hebrew 'my God is Yahweh'.
Aleyna: Turkish, probably 'light' or 'moon glow'; also a variant of Alina. Origin uncertain.
Elizabeth: Greek form of Hebrew Elisheva, 'my God is an oath'.
Lilya: Russian form of Lily; also Slavic 'lily'.
Omer: Arabic 'Umar, 'long-lived, flourishing'; also Hebrew 'sheaf of grain'. Also a Flemish saint's name.
Kevin: Anglicised Irish Caoimhín, from caomh 'kind, gentle' and gein 'birth'. Saint Kevin of Glendalough.
Aurore: French, 'dawn', from Latin aurora. The Roman goddess of dawn.
Enora: Breton, from the Breton form of Honorine or Honora, from Latin honor.
Elle: From French 'she', or a short form of Eleanor or Ellen. Also Scandinavian 'elf'.
Madeleine: French form of Magdalene, 'from Magdala', a town by the Sea of Galilee.
Aymen: Variant of Arabic Ayman, 'right-handed, blessed, lucky'.
Mamadou: West African form of Mohammed, Arabic 'praiseworthy'.
Kayla: Modern English, probably from Kaila or Kayla, possibly a form of Katherine or Hebrew 'crown'. Origin uncertain.
Miro: Slavic, from mir 'peace, world'. Also Spanish 'I look'.
Kai: Several origins: Hawaiian 'sea', Frisian and Scandinavian pet form of Kaj or Gaius, Welsh 'keeper of the keys'.
Mahir: Arabic, 'skilled, talented'. Also Turkish form of Maher.
Naïl: Arabic Nail, 'one who attains, achiever'. French spelling.
Athéna: French form of Athena, the Greek goddess of wisdom. Origin of the name itself is pre-Greek.
Junayd: Arabic, diminutive of jund 'soldier, army'. Famous Sufi Junayd of Baghdad.
Cériel: Flemish form of Cyriel, from Greek kyrios 'lord'. Variant of Cyril.
Oussaid: Probably a Moroccan or Berber form of Arabic Usaid, 'little lion'. Origin uncertain.
Chiara: Italian, 'clear, bright', from Latin clarus. Saint Clare's name.
Sebastian: From Latin Sebastianus, 'of Sebaste', from Greek sebastos 'venerable'.
Roan: Irish Ruadhán, 'little red-haired one'. Also English 'roan' colour or a rowan tree.
Viggo: Scandinavian, from Old Norse vig 'war, battle'.
Camila: Spanish and Portuguese form of Camilla, Latin, a young attendant at a sacrifice; meaning uncertain.
Isaiah: Hebrew Yeshayahu, 'salvation of the Lord'. A biblical prophet.
Élise: French short form of Elisabeth, Hebrew 'my God is an oath'.
Hanne: Danish, Dutch and German short form of Johanne or Hanna. Hebrew 'grace'.
Laure: French form of Laura, from Latin laurus 'laurel'.
Aïcha: French spelling of Arabic Aisha, 'alive, living'.
Paolo: Italian form of Paul, from Latin Paulus, 'small, humble'.
Lize: Dutch short form of Elisabeth, Hebrew 'my God is an oath'. Also a variant of Liese.
Matthew: English form of Matthias, from Hebrew Mattityahu, 'gift of God'.
Nathanaël: French form of Nathanael, Hebrew 'God has given'. Biblical disciple.
Atlas: Greek, from the Titan who held the sky, probably 'bearer, enduring'. Also a modern name.
Mayssa: Arabic Maysa, 'proudly swaying, walking gracefully'. French spelling.
Sep: Flemish short form of Josephus or Sebastiaan.
Camélia: French, from the camellia flower, named after Georg Kamel, a Jesuit botanist.
Edgar: English, from Old English ead 'wealth, fortune' and gar 'spear'.
Maysa: Arabic, 'proud, graceful in gait'. Also a modern name.
Céril: Flemish variant of Cyriel or Cyril, from Greek kyrios 'lord'.
Matthias: Greek form of Hebrew Mattityahu, 'gift of God'. Apostle chosen to replace Judas.
Tibo: Flemish and Dutch short form of Thibault, from Germanic 'bold people'.
Salomé: French form of Salome, Hebrew shalom 'peace'. Biblical figure.
Daoud: Arabic form of David, from Hebrew 'beloved'.
Liz: Short form of Elizabeth, Hebrew 'my God is an oath'.
Kamil: Arabic, 'perfect, complete'. Also Polish and Czech form of Camillus.
Zainab: Arabic, 'fragrant tree' or 'father's jewel'. Daughter of the Prophet.
Mark: English form of Latin Marcus, probably from Mars, the Roman war god.
Bastien: French short form of Sébastien, from Greek sebastos 'venerable'.
Lauren: English and French feminine form of Laurence, from Latin laurus, 'laurel'.
Nel: Short form of Cornelia, Helen or Eleonora. Also a Polish and Dutch pet name.
Nisa: Arabic 'women', or a Turkish variant of Nisan, 'April'. Also a Hebrew 'miracle' form.
Rafaël: French and Dutch form of Raphael, Hebrew 'God has healed'.
Zahra: Arabic, 'radiant, shining flower'. Title of Fatima, the Prophet's daughter.
Lily-Rose: Compound of Lily and Rose, both flower names, from Latin lilium and rosa. Popularised by Lily-Rose Depp.
Bob: Short form of Robert, Germanic hrod 'fame' and beraht 'bright'.
Eymen: Turkish form of Arabic Ayman, 'right-handed, blessed'.
Damian: From Greek Damianos, from damazo 'to tame, subdue'. Saint Damian was a healer.
Boaz: Hebrew, possibly 'in him is strength' or 'swiftness'. Biblical husband of Ruth.
Niya: Several: Persian 'ancestor', Hebrew 'purpose' or Swahili 'intention'. Modern variant; origin varies.
Kylian: French form of Killian, Irish Cillian, probably 'little church' or 'bright-headed'. Saint Kilian.
Eléna: Variant of Elena, form of Helen, Greek 'torch' or 'bright one'.
Luis: Spanish and German form of Louis, from Germanic hlud 'famous' and wig 'battle'.
Yasmin: From Persian yasmin, the jasmine flower.
Lisette: French diminutive of Elisabeth, Hebrew 'my God is an oath'.
Michael: Hebrew, 'who is like God?'. An archangel.
Melina: Greek, possibly 'honey' from meli, or a form of Melinda. Also an Italian name from Latin.
Feline: Dutch, from Latin felinus 'cat-like', or a Dutch form of Felicity. Probably a modern use.
Layla: Arabic, 'night'. Famous from the classic love story of Layla and Majnun.
Hope: English virtue name, from Old English hopa. Used since the Puritan era.
Gustave: French, from Swedish Gustav, probably Germanic 'staff of the Goths' or 'god's staff'.
Rocco: Italian, from Germanic hroc 'rest' or 'rook'. Saint Roch is protector against plague.
Thieu: Dutch Limburg short form of Mathieu or Matthieu, from Hebrew 'gift of God'.
Ruben: Hebrew Reuven, 'behold, a son'. Biblical eldest son of Jacob.
Jasper: English and Dutch form of Gaspar, from Persian 'treasurer'. One of the three Magi.
Pierre: French form of Peter, from Greek petros 'stone, rock'.
Floor: Dutch short form of Florentina or Florence, from Latin florens 'blooming'.
Yassir: Variant of Arabic Yasir, 'easy, wealthy, prosperous'.
Alia: Arabic Aliyah, 'exalted, noble'. Also Hebrew 'ascent' and Latin 'other'.
Yassin: Variant of Arabic Yasin, a chapter of the Quran; its meaning is uncertain.
Zaynab: Arabic, 'fragrant tree' or 'father's jewel'. Daughter of the Prophet Muhammad.
Souleymane: West African and French spelling of Sulayman, from Hebrew Solomon, 'peace'.
Bonnie: Scottish, from Scots bonnie 'pretty, good'. Probably from French bon.
Lynn: English, from Welsh llyn 'lake'. Also a short form of Linda or Caroline.
Alessandro: Italian form of Alexander, from Greek 'defender of men'.
Filip: Slavic, Dutch and Scandinavian form of Philip, from Greek 'friend of horses'.
Léopold: French form of Leopold, from Germanic leud 'people' and bald 'bold'.
Santiago: Spanish, from Sant Iago, Saint James; form of Hebrew Jacob, 'supplanter'.
Louie: English diminutive of Louis, from Germanic 'famous in battle'.
Suzie: English pet form of Susan, from Hebrew Shoshannah, 'lily'.
Robbe: Flemish pet form of Robert, Germanic hrod 'fame' and beraht 'bright'.
Astrid: Scandinavian, from Old Norse Ástríðr, 'divinely beautiful' or 'divine strength'.
Safa: Arabic, 'purity, clarity'. Also the name of a hill in Mecca.
Selim: Turkish and Arabic, 'safe, sound, peaceful'. Name of Ottoman sultans.
Noud: Dutch short form of Arnoud or Arnold, from Germanic 'eagle' and 'rule'.
Arlo: English, of uncertain origin; possibly from Old English 'fortified hill' or Spanish. Origin uncertain.
Michelle: French feminine of Michel, from Hebrew 'who is like God?'.
Kenza: Arabic Kanza, 'treasure'. Popular in North Africa.
Enes: Turkish form of Arabic Anas, 'friendliness, companionship'.
Eléa: Probably a modern French form of Hélène or Elia. Origin uncertain.
Evy: Short form of Eva or Evelien, from Hebrew Chavah, 'life'.
Dante: Italian short form of Durante, from Latin durans 'enduring'. Italian poet.
Joy: English, from Old French joie, from Latin gaudium.
Esmee: Dutch form of Esmé, from Old French 'esteemed, loved'.
Ruby: English, from the red gemstone, from Latin rubeus 'red'.
Julot: French diminutive of Jules, from Latin Julius; Belgian pet form.
Nand: Dutch short form of Ferdinand, Germanic 'journey' and 'bold'. Also Sanskrit 'joy'.
Fenna: Frisian short form of Fenne or Josephine, possibly Germanic. Origin uncertain.
Edward: English, from Old English ead 'wealth' and weard 'guardian'.
Elia: Italian and Hebrew, from Elijah, 'my God is Yahweh'.
Eleanor: Probably from Provençal Aliénor, or Greek 'torch' via Helen. Origin uncertain.
Diane: French form of Diana, Roman goddess of the hunt.
Cyril: From Greek Kyrillos, from kyrios 'lord'. Saint Cyril, Slavic apostle.
Selma: Possibly from Arabic 'safe', Celtic 'fair view' or a short form of Anselma. Origin uncertain.
Mylan: Probably a modern coinage, similar to Milan or Mylan from Slavic mil 'dear'. Origin uncertain.
Israa: Arabic Isra, 'night journey', referring to Muhammad's journey in the Quran.
Jaxx: Modern coinage, a variant of Jax or Jackson, 'son of Jack'. Origin uncertain.
Milana: Slavic, feminine of Milan, from mil 'dear, gracious'. Also an Italian form from Milan.
Odil: Flemish form of Odilo, from Germanic aud 'wealth'.
Guillaume: French form of William, from Germanic wil 'will' and helm 'helmet'.
Denis: French form of Dionysius, Greek god of wine. Saint Denis.
Léana: Probably a modern French blend, from Léa or Léna. Origin uncertain.
Roxane: French form of Roxana, from Persian Roshanak, 'dawn' or 'little star'.
Teo: Short form of Teodoro or Matteo; Greek theos 'god'. Also Teodor.
Ediz: Turkish, apparently from 'high, tall'; possibly a modern coinage. Origin uncertain.
Mayson: Modern English, from Mason, an occupation name 'stonemason'. Variant spelling.
Anaya: Sanskrit 'without a guide', or Arabic 'caring'. Also a Hindu name meaning 'caring'. Meaning varies.
Elyana: Probably a modern blend of Eliana and Elyan. Hebrew 'my God has answered'. Origin uncertain.
Jan: Dutch, Slavic and Scandinavian form of John, from Hebrew 'God is gracious'.
Loris: Italian and French, perhaps a short form of Lorenzo or Hilaire. Origin uncertain.
Héloïse: French, from Germanic Helewidis, perhaps 'healthy' and 'wide'. Famous medieval Héloïse.
Line: Danish, Norwegian and French short form of Caroline or Pauline. Also Dutch 'line'.
Nona: Latin, 'ninth'. Also a short form of Antonia.
Loan: Breton and French, probably a form of Loïc or Yoann. Origin uncertain.
Josephine: French feminine of Joseph, Hebrew 'he will add'.
Loïs: French form of Louis, or a variant of Lois. Probably from Germanic 'famous warrior'.
Hayden: English, from Old English heg 'hay' and denu 'valley'. A surname turned given name.
Jerom: Dutch form of Jerome, from Greek Hieronymos, 'sacred name'.
Manoé: French form of Manoah, Hebrew 'rest'; also a modern variant of Noé. Origin uncertain.
Archie: Short form of Archibald, from Germanic ercan 'genuine' and bald 'bold'.
